annotation.material_differences: Response A makes a stronger and more specific commitment to resolve the issue quickly and says it will be fixed soon / in the next day or two, while also saying it would check back if anything changes. Responses B and C similarly give a rough timeline, but B adds that the estimate is given mainly to give something concrete and C omits any interim-status follow-up, limiting follow-up to the final resolution. These differences affect expectation management and the follow-up mechanism.
annotation.equivalence_rationale: All three responses generally reassure the customer and avoid fully diagnosing the root cause, but they do not preserve the same operational commitments. The follow-up criterion is materially different because A offers to check back on changes, while B and C explicitly restrict contact until the final fix. The expectation-management criterion also differs because A promises a quicker resolution more definitively, whereas B frames the estimate as a concrete placeholder and C is slightly less explicit. These differences could change how the response would be judged on clear explanation, expectation management, and follow-up.
